name: Mechanical Engineer (BS)

rules.name: Mathematics and Science (45 units combined)

children.name: Mathematics
children.desc:
The program requires a minimum of 45 units of math and science combined, including 24 units in math and 20 units in science. The 45th unit may be either math or science. ACE units do not count toward major program unit minimums, though they do count toward the 180-unit minimum needed for graduation.
The CME courses in mathematics are strongly preferred for ME majors.

children.name: Calculus
children.notes:
10 units of AP Calculus BC, with placement into course/course, is equivalent to course/course/course and acceptable in any engineering major. If 6-8 units of AP or IB credit are given, course must be taken regardless of the Math Diagnostic Placement results.
Recommended Timeline: Taken in the 1st year.

children.name: Science

children.notes:

children.notes:

children.name: Additional Science Courses

rules.name: Honors Overview
rules.desc:
Honors programs are designed to allow undergraduates with strong academic records and enthusiasm for independent research to engage in a significant project leading to a degree with departmental honors. This option is particularly valuable for students who plan to pursue a PhD because it provides research experience that helps prepare for doctoral-level work. These programs require that the student find a faculty member from the Academic Council in the School of Engineering to supervise the work, in addition to a second reader.
The Department of Mechanical Engineering offers a program leading to a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering with Honors. This program provides a unique opportunity for qualified mechanical engineering majors to conduct independent study and research at an advanced level with a faculty mentor.
Honors Criteria

• GPA of 3.5 or higher in the major

• Arrangement with an ME faculty member who agrees to be the thesis advisor; the advisor must be a member of the Academic Council

• Apply no later than the end of the second week of the autumn quarter of your senior year
To receive departmental honors, students admitted to the honors program must, in addition to satisfying the standard requirements for the undergraduate degree, do the following:

• Declare the honors program in Axess

• Maintain a 3.5 GPA in the major required for admission to the honors program

• Under the direction of the thesis advisor, complete at least nine units of ME 191H during the senior year

• Complete an honors thesis deemed acceptable by the thesis advisor and at least one additional faculty member

rules.name: GPA of 3.5 or higher in the major
Honors thesis accepted by the advisor and a second faculty member

gpa: The minimum GPA for all courses taken for the major is 2.7. This includes Math, Science, TiS, Fundamentals, Depth, and Technical Electives.
grading:
• All courses taken for the major must be taken for a letter grade if this option is offered by the instructor.

• The minimum grade for all courses taken for the major is a C. This includes Math, Science, TiS, Fundamentals, Depth, and Technical Electives.
policies:
• All courses taken for the major can be listed only under one category — no double-counting of course units is allowed.

• All courses taken for the major must be taken in prerequisite order.

• To satisfy ABET requirements for graduation, if a course requirement is satisfied without conferral of units (for example, waiving a course using SoE procedures), the Math and Science units requirements must still be met by taking additional courses from the SoE approved course lists.

• To satisfy ABET requirements for graduation, the combined units from Fundamentals, Core, and Technical Electives must be at least 68 units.

• Any deviations to the outline program must be approved by the ME Student Services Office. Visit Undergraduate Course Petitions on the ME Student Intranet for instructions.
transferPolicy:
Transfer and AP/IB credits in Math, Science, Fundamentals, and TiS must be approved by the SoE Dean’s Office. Visit Transfers-AP-Exceptions on the SoE Undergrad Handbook for instructions.
Transfer credits in Mechanical Engineering Depth and Technical Electives must be approved by the ME Student Services Office. Visit Undergraduate Course Petitions on the ME Student Intranet for instructions.
